Hello Professor [Last name],

My name is Vinil Polepalli and I am an undergraduate at New York University, where I am studying Computer Science and Business. I have been a research intern in the Chiosis Lab at Memorial Sloan Kettering, where I built protein-ligand graph neural networks for Hsp90 and epichaperome complexes and reached 0.984 ROC AUC separating active from inactive inhibitor candidates.

[Three or four sentences showing I actually read one of their papers. Name something specific from it: the method, the result, the dataset, the limitation. Add a second concrete detail. Then say what I would extend, try next, or apply it to, and how, connected to my own work.]

In the past, I have worked on the following related projects:
- Sole author on cVAE-augmented deep learning for pan-cancer RNA-seq classification, about 98% test accuracy across 5 cancer types: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.02743
- Hsp90 inhibitor virtual screening in the Chiosis Lab at Memorial Sloan Kettering, 4,566 candidates screened at 0.984 GNN ROC AUC and 5x enrichment: https://hsp90-dashboard.vercel.app/
- Semantic segmentation for UAV-based environmental monitoring at Carnegie Mellon Robotics Institute, 0.88 mean IoU and 0.94 F1 on 25,000 labeled aerial images

I have extensively used PyTorch and Python in past work, along with molecular docking and graph neural network tooling, but have a lot of coding experience and am adaptable to whichever libraries your lab utilizes. Please let me know if there is a fit in your lab.

I would be happy to elaborate on my skills and where I think I can best help out.

Thank you!

--
Vinil Polepalli
